name: Rigoni di Asiago Fiordifrutta Organic Fruit Spread (Wild Blueberry / Cherry)
ingredients_found: Organic wild blueberries, organic apple juice (concentrate), fruit pectin. No added sugar; sweetened only with organic apple juice.
reason: Whole organic fruit + organic apple-juice sweetening + traditional fruit pectin; zero cane sugar, seed oils, gums, dyes, or preservatives.
justification: A fruit-only preserve with an intact whole-food glycemic matrix (P4) and no mucosal-disrupting emulsifiers/gums (P1); pectin is a native gelling agent, not a disqualifying gum.
notes: Sweetener is fruit juice only; both flavors follow the same fruit + apple-juice + pectin formula.

name: Chia Smash Superfood Fruit Spread (Raspberry / Wild Blueberry)
ingredients_found: Raspberries, dates, chia seeds, lemon juice concentrate, fruit pectin, rowanberry extract.
reason: Whole-fruit + date sweetening with whole chia seeds for structure; zero added refined sugar, seed oils, gums, dyes, or preservatives.
justification: Sweetened by whole fruit and dates (Tier-1 sweetener) inside an intact fiber matrix (P4); chia adds native fiber with no emulsifier/gum load (P1).
notes: Rowanberry extract is a natural fruit extract, not a synthetic additive.

name: St. Dalfour Fruit Spread (Fig Royale / Wild Blueberry)
ingredients_found: Figs, fruit juice concentrates (grape and date), lemon juice, fruit pectin. No cane sugar, no artificial ingredients.
reason: Fruit-only preserve sweetened by grape/date juice concentrate with lemon juice and fruit pectin; zero cane sugar, corn syrup, seed oils, gums, or preservatives.
justification: Whole fruit + fruit-juice sweetening delivers a native glycemic matrix (P4); traditional kettle cooking with pectin only, no mucosal disruptors (P1).
notes: Fruit juice concentrate composition can vary slightly by flavor; both audited variants are cane-sugar-free.

name: Crofter's Organic "Just Fruit" Spread (Strawberry / Apricot)
ingredients_found: Organic apple juice concentrate, organic strawberries, apple pectin, ascorbic acid (vitamin C), citric acid.
reason: 100% fruit-juice sweetened organic spread; zero cane sugar, seed oils, gums, synthetic dyes, or preservatives.
justification: Fruit-juice sweetening keeps sugar inside a whole-food matrix (P4); ascorbic/citric acid are benign acidulants, not gut-disrupting emulsifiers (P1).
notes: Apricot variant uses the same apple-juice + fruit + pectin base.

name: World of Chia Raspberry Fruit Spread
ingredients_found: Raspberries, organic agave nectar, organic chia seeds, lime juice.
reason: Clean deck with whole chia for structure, but sweetened primarily with organic agave nectar (a refined natural syrup) rather than whole fruit, honey, or maple.
justification: Agave is not a disqualifier (not HFCS, synthetic, or polyol) so it passes the pre-filter, but as a refined high-fructose syrup it is not a Tier-1 whole-fruit/honey sweetener and delivers a faster glycemic influx (P4); no gums or seed oils (P1).
notes: Agave nectar is outside the explicit Tier-1/2/3 sweetener whitelist; placed at Tier 3 as a clean, non-disqualifying natural syrup rather than a whole-food sweetener.

name: Crofter's Organic Premium Spread (Strawberry / Berry Harvest)
ingredients_found: Organic strawberries, organic cane sugar, natural apple pectin, ascorbic acid (vitamin C), citric acid.
reason: Clean organic cane-sugar fruit preserve; zero seed oils, gums, synthetic dyes, or preservatives.
justification: Organic unrefined cane sugar is the Tier-3 allowed sweetener in an inherently-sweet category (P4); otherwise a clean fruit + pectin matrix with no mucosal disruptors (P1).

name: H-E-B More Fruit Strawberry Fruit Spread
ingredients_found: Strawberries, sugar, water, less than 2% of: fruit pectin, citric acid, carob bean gum, black carrot juice concentrate.
reason: Carob bean (locust bean) gum — an L3 disqualifying emulsifier/gum on the banned gum list.
justification: Carob/locust bean gum acts as a surfactant that strips the intestinal mucin layer and compromises tight junctions (P1), triggering an automatic L3 disqualification regardless of the otherwise clean fruit base.
notes: Prior audit flagged 'dye' incorrectly — the color is black carrot juice concentrate (natural), not a synthetic dye; the true disqualifier is carob bean gum, which the prior audit missed.

name: Smucker's Simply Fruit Spread (Strawberry / Apricot)
ingredients_found: Fruit syrup, strawberries, fruit pectin, lemon juice concentrate, red grape juice concentrate (for color), natural flavor.
reason: Fruit-only sweetened (fruit syrup / juice concentrate); zero cane sugar, HFCS, seed oils, gums, or synthetic dyes.
justification: Sweetened solely by fruit juice/syrup inside a fruit + pectin matrix (P4), with color from natural grape juice concentrate; no emulsifiers or gums that would disrupt the mucosal barrier (P1).
notes: Contains 'natural flavor,' a minor non-whole-food marker, but no disqualifying additive; both strawberry and apricot variants are cane-sugar-free.

name: Good Good No Added Sugar Strawberry Jam
ingredients_found: Strawberries (58%), water, sweeteners (erythritol, stevia extract), fruit pectin, rowanberry extract, lemon powder, citric acid, carrot-blackcurrant concentrate (for color), ascorbic acid.
reason: Erythritol (polyol) plus stevia blended with erythritol — both TRASH conditions under the Sweetener Matrix.
justification: Erythritol is an unfermentable polyol that reaches the colon and drives osmotic water shifts and bacterial fermentation (P5/P1), and stevia blended with a polyol is explicitly disqualified by the Sweetener Matrix.

name: Bonne Maman Apricot Preserves
ingredients_found: Apricots, sugar, brown cane sugar, concentrated lemon juice, fruit pectin. No HFCS, no artificial coloring/flavors, no preservatives.
reason: Clean cane-sugar fruit preserve; zero seed oils, gums, synthetic dyes, or preservatives.
justification: A clean fruit + cane-sugar + pectin preserve passes every pre-filter; added cane sugar is not auto-trashed in an inherently-sweet category and places it at the Tier-3 sweetener level (P4), with no mucosal disruptors (P1).
notes: Prior audit flagged 'emul' — incorrect; the deck contains fruit pectin only, no gums or emulsifiers.

name: Polaner Sugar Free with Fiber Strawberry Preserves
ingredients_found: Water, strawberries, maltodextrin, polydextrose, fruit pectin, citric acid, guar gum, natural flavor, sucralose, potassium sorbate and sodium benzoate (to preserve freshness), calcium chloride, Red 40.
reason: Red 40 synthetic dye and sodium benzoate (L2), plus sucralose (synthetic sweetener), guar gum (L3), and polydextrose (engineered fiber filler).
justification: Multiple hard disqualifiers stack here — an L2 petroleum dye and chemical preservative alongside an L3 synthetic sweetener, gum, and engineered fiber — hitting the gut barrier (P1), glycemic (P4), and preservative-load axes simultaneously.
notes: Textbook UPF 'sugar free' trap; highest severity cited is L2 (Red 40 / sodium benzoate).

name: Welch's Concord Grape Jelly
ingredients_found: Concord grapes, corn syrup, high fructose corn syrup, fruit pectin, citric acid, sodium citrate.
reason: High fructose corn syrup (and corn syrup) as the primary sweeteners — an explicit jam-category disqualifier.
justification: HFCS floods the hepatic portal vein with fructose absent any protective fiber/protein matrix, maximizing de novo lipogenesis and insulin spikes (P4); an engineered sweetener substrate with no whole-food value.
